solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Profession of one into endemic outbreak

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so one piece is placed within another
an outbreak is a sudden eruption, so the letters burst out of their order

explanation.surface: A health worker's job is to go into a region where a disease outbreak has taken hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endemic outbreak' sounds like an epidemic to be treated, which fits the surface neatly, but outbreak is just the shuffle signal for the word before it with I added.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicine is the calling of doctors, a recognised professional career alongside law and the church.

clue.text: Seldom struck poses

indicators.note: something struck is knocked about, so its letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone rarely strikes a pose, as if shy in front of the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struck poses' reads as a single phrase, striking a pose; the verb belongs to the anagram and 'poses' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To model is to sit or stand for an artist or photographer, so models works as a verb meaning holds a posture.

clue.text: Error indeed having failed an obligation

indicators.note: the preposition places the first thing inside the second, so one word sits within another

parts.note: read as two words, the second being an act or action
a fault is a mistake or error

explanation.surface: A mistake was made, and indeed the obligation went unmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed' is read as two words, 'in deed', so the error sits inside the deed.
explanation.definitionFit: To default is to fail to pay a debt or meet a duty, so defaulted describes a borrower who did not fulfil a commitment.

clue.text: Greek philosopher needs no outside help to find this box

indicators.note: doing without the outside means the edges are stripped away, and 'no' also asks for the round zero letter to go

explanation.surface: An ancient thinker is so self-sufficient he needs nobody's help to find a box.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outer S at each end of SOCRATES, and 'no' (O, a zero) also goes, leaving CRATE. The deletion is loose, so lean on the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crate is a wooden packing case, a large container used for carrying goods.

clue.text: Sunrise over cryptic clue's central element

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from bottom to top, so the letters turn round
in a down entry one piece lies over and around another, enclosing it

parts.note: the star itself, before the rest of the word acts on it

indicators.note: cryptic means hidden or puzzling, so the letters are disguised by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter's riddle about dawn hides some key ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunrise' looks like dawn, but it splits into the star and a signal to turn it upward; in a down clue 'over' means sitting on top, here wrapping round.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the core or heart of something, the part at the middle around which the rest gathers.

clue.text: Evil wicked sailor

explanation.surface: A villainous seaman, nasty through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evil wicked' look like two adjectives describing the sailor; each is a piece of the name instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad is the legendary seafarer of the Arabian Nights tales, famous for his seven voyages.

clue.text: Recluse is home and dry to welcome traveller

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A hermit stays at home and off the drink, yet still takes in a passing wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' means teetotal, abbreviated TT, someone who drinks no alcohol; 'home and' is a charade, the second part swallowing the traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert is a shy, inward-looking person who prefers solitude, close to a recluse who withdraws from society.

clue.text: Most of seafood served in a bowl

indicators.note: most of something is all but a little, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: only the first three letters work here: the Baltic is a sea of northern Europe

explanation.surface: Fish and shellfish dished up in a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seafood' must be split: the sea supplies the wordplay and 'food' begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spicy curry cooked and served in a wok-like metal dish, also called a balti, popular in Birmingham.

clue.text: Instead, sat up with record stores

indicators.note: things that are up in the air or stirred up are in disorder, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: read as 'in stead', keeping the second word

explanation.surface: Rather than going to bed, someone stayed up late with the archives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instead' reads as 'in stead', putting STEAD and SAT in a stirred-up state; 'record stores' is the definition, collections of records.
explanation.definitionFit: Datasets are organised collections of data, places where records are kept for computing and analysis.

clue.text: Editor backing one engaged in opposition

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: ED is the standard abbreviation for editor
a man who is engaged to be married

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor supports someone involved in resisting authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like supporting the next person, but it turns the editor round; 'one engaged' is a husband-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance or refusal to obey, a stance of standing against someone.

clue.text: Design primarily thin metal probe

parts.note: a style is a design or fashion

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: An engineer's brief: mainly a slender metal instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' seems to qualify 'design' as a whole, but it picks only the first letter of the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylet is a slender surgical instrument or wire inserted into tubes, a fine probe used by doctors.

clue.text: Value one's life talent, initially showing some potential

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Prize your gifts, since early talent reveals what you might become.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potential' reads as promise or ability; here it is electrical potential, measured in a unit of one.
explanation.definitionFit: The volt is the unit of electric potential difference, so one volt is a quantity of electrical potential.

clue.text: Large river parasite

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A big waterway infested by a bloodsucking creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire (and another in Sussex), a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a small wingless insect living on the skin or hair of animals and feeding off its host.

clue.text: Ultimately broke, funny people must take on money matters

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept
to take something on is to take it aboard, so a piece goes inside another

explanation.surface: Penniless comedians will have to start dealing with their finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take on' sounds like accepting a task, but it means taking ON inside the comics, just after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Economics is the study of wealth, trade and finance, so it concerns all questions about cash.

clue.text: Keeps soup ingredients

definitions.meaning: first meaning: holds goods for sale, as a shop does
second meaning: broths made by simmering bones and vegetables

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it sounds like preserving soup ingredients; the two halves are separate meanings, a verb and a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop that keeps an item carries it on its shelves, and cooks use flavoured liquids made from bones as soup bases.

clue.text: Conran's first interior design set standard

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter only of the name
to design is to arrange anew, so the letters are given a new layout

explanation.surface: Terence Conran's pioneering interiors set the benchmark for others.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Terence Conran was a British designer and founder of the Habitat shops, which makes 'interior design' look like a plain phrase rather than fodder and a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion is a principle or benchmark by which things are judged, the same idea as a standard.

clue.text: Nothing beats this old city: capital of Turkmenistan

parts.note: Thebes was an ancient city in Egypt, and another in Greece

indicators.note: a capital is a head letter, so the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A travel boast: no ancient city can rival Ashgabat, the Turkmen capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Turkmenistan' tempts you to recall Ashgabat; it only means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbeaten by anything else is supreme, top of the pile, unrivalled by all competitors.

clue.text: Finally vote Green: different movement, full of vigour

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter is kept
different means changed, so the letters are put in a changed order

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: An election slogan: in the end, back the Greens, a different and lively political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' and 'movement' suggest an environmental campaign; one is fodder and the other a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Energetic means lively and dynamic, describing someone with lots of drive and stamina.

clue.text: Decade left in knots

indicators.note: the preposition places the first piece inside the second

explanation.surface: Ten years of being tied up in knots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as the opposite of right, or as remaining; here it is the past tense of leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenties is a decade, as in the 1920s, a ten-year span such as a person's age from twenty to twenty-nine.

clue.text: You and I would sound bells for such an occasion

parts.note: we'd is short for we would
to ding is to ring like a bell

explanation.surface: A couple says they would have the church bells rung for their big day.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints a church ceremony, so the definition is apt; 'You and I would' is the contraction we'd, dropping its apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is a marriage ceremony, a celebratory event at which church bells traditionally ring out.

clue.text: Network sending up brief threnody

indicators.note: in a down clue sending something up makes it read from bottom to top
brief means cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a threnody is a lament, a dirge

explanation.surface: A TV channel mocks a short funeral lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sending up' sounds like satire, but in a down clue it turns the word upward; the lament loses its last letter first.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a network of lines crossing at right angles, or the national system of power cables.

clue.text: Tom's number one wine-tasting note

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
number one is nursery slang for urination

explanation.surface: Someone named Tom has a favourite description when sampling wines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like top choice; it is the childish euphemism. The phrase really is used by wine critics, especially of Sauvignon Blanc.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasters describe a pungent, sharp aroma in some white wines by that name, a recognised if rude descriptor.

clue.text: Fall of lawsuit involving rogue

indicators.note: to involve is to include or wrap in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a case is a legal action

explanation.surface: A legal action against a scoundrel collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' suggests a downfall in court; it is a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a small waterfall, water tumbling down rocks in stages.

clue.text: Set theory ignoring the ground floor

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so those letters are removed
ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and remixed

parts.note: the word with its opening three letters removed

explanation.surface: A mathematician's set theory leaves out the building's lowest level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground floor' is a single idea in the surface, but 'ground' is the anagram signal and 'floor' alone defines; 'the' is removed from the start of theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one level of a building, the British spelling of what Americans call a story.

clue.text: Where youngsters may be, run back all episodes

indicators.note: going back means heading in the opposite direction, so letters are read in reverse

explanation.surface: A TV schedule note: wherever the kids are, repeat the whole box set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run back' reads as a rerun of a show, which fits 'all episodes'; it is RUN turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurseries are rooms or schools where small children are cared for, places for infants and toddlers.

clue.text: Commodious jumper? That's surprising!

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumping animal

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished at how baggy a sweater is.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater, which suits a roomy garment, but here it is a leaping kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Commodious means spacious, having plenty of space inside, the same as roomy.

clue.text: A couple of other things said before bedtime

parts.note: asks for two copies of the next word

indicators.note: other means different, so the letters are made into something different

explanation.surface: A child asks for a few more things just before going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A couple of other things' sounds like stalling at bedtime; take two of the word thing and rearrange each into the bedtime farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled phrase is the affectionate goodnight wish parents say to children as they go to sleep.

clue.text: See 25
Quintessential writer with a pointed shape

parts.note: the setter, as the writer of the clue, refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: The archetypal author sporting a sharp, tapered look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' tempts you toward PEN or an author's name; it is the setter speaking as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iconic is a perfect representative example, the very essence of its kind, as quintessential means.

clue.text: 16, 1 across afterwards admits this is foul

definitions.note: the cross-references make the saying 'laughter is the best medicine', so the answer is what that is

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Taking the best medicine and later declaring that it tastes horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is THE BEST and 1 across MEDICINE; the proverb says laughter is the best medicine. 'This is foul' is what someone says, so it is the disgusted cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that cheerful amusement heals better than any remedy, making mirth the finest cure.

clue.text: Adage that Yang is failing and its opposite is in decline

indicators.note: something failing is breaking down, so its letters fall apart and regroup

parts.words: and its opposite is in decline
parts.note: surface padding that also works as a second route: the opposite of yang inside sag

explanation.surface: A proverb claims that yang is weakening while yin also slips away.
explanation.walkthrough: There is a second wordplay in the clue: the opposite of yang, YIN, inside SAG (decline) also gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a traditional proverb, a short well-known expression of a general truth.

clue.text: State of knowledge cut back before bank holiday ends

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters are read in reverse
ends are the extremities, so the last letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: Our understanding was trimmed just before the long weekend finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of knowledge' looks like a single phrase, but 'State' alone is the definition. A bank holiday is a British public holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentucky is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the south-east of the country.
